tasks.title: Draft and implement test oracle asserting bwrap-jailed, net-unshared, lockfile-only dependency installation
acceptance_criteria: Imports the module/symbols via importlib spec (loader.exec_module) from tmp_path rather than raw exec or __import__.
Correctly injects mock jail_runner and pip_installer seams to capture install arguments without actual subprocess or jail calls.
Asserts positive case: normal lockfile installation runs in jail and captures --unshare-net, and the re-run uses the installed deps dir on PYTHONPATH.
Asserts negative control: an attacker-controlled ModuleNotFoundError in stderr does NOT trigger installation of that package name, and the un-jailed host-side pip install is never called.
Asserts lockfile-only: the installer uses '-r' and the path to the resolved requirements lockfile, never a bare package name.
Asserts fail-closed: detonation fails closed and performs no host network install if no lockfile is found or if bwrap is missing.
Includes at least 2 regression tests asserting no change to existing smoke or lockfile-free detonation verdicts.

spec.objective: Author a non-vacuous RED test suite under tests/ngv2/test_poc_runner_jailed_install.py to verify that dependency installation during detonation is jailed, lockfile-only, net-unshared, and fail-closed, preventing remote code execution via attacker-influenced stderr package names.
functional_requirements: Author test cases asserting (a) POSITIVE: a normal lockfile install succeeds in a net-unshared jail, and the re-run uses the installed deps dir on PYTHONPATH.
Author test cases asserting (b) NEGATIVE CONTROL: an attacker-named package appearing in the PoC's stderr is never installed, and the host subprocess.run is not called with it.
Author test cases asserting (c) LOCKFILE-ONLY: the install command runs against a lockfile via -r <lockfile>, not a bare package name.
Author test cases asserting (d) FAIL-CLOSED: if no lockfile is found or bwrap is unavailable, the installation fails and detonation does not fall back to a host network install.
spec.interfaces: Injectable seams: pip_installer, jail_runner callables to detonate_live. Target file imports: importlib based loading of ngv2/poc_runner_live.py.
edge_cases: Requirements files: text/dev/lock files. The target repo_root has requirements.txt, requirements-dev.txt, or requirements.lock.
bwrap missing: shutil.which('bwrap') returns None or is unavailable, causing the installer to return False and prevent installation.
non_goals: Do not wire this into a live run_hunt or conductor traversal. No FSM or worker changes.
Do not change success/verdict gate logic.
spec.implementation_notes: Imports must use importlib.util.spec_from_file_location and module_from_spec to load the target code. Real subprocess.run must be monkeypatched to raise an exception to catch any unmocked host execution.

test_spec.test_data_requirements: Requires mock target repository files containing requirements.txt, requirements-dev.txt, requirements.lock, or none to test lockfile resolution, plus mock stderr streams containing ModuleNotFoundError.

token_budget_ratio.note: Test-only task: requires no implementation tokens; test tokens allocated to cover robust oracle authoring.

tasks.title: Implement bwrap-jailed, network-unshared, lockfile-only dependency installer
acceptance_criteria: Changes both _default_pip_installer and detonate_live to implement jailed lockfile-only dependency installs.

Ensures _default_pip_installer: (i) resolves requirements.txt, requirements-dev.txt, or requirements.lock in order from the target's repo_root, (ii) constructs the jailed pip install command utilizing build_detonation_jail_argv, unsharing network, and mapping the venv/target_dir writable, and (iii) returns False (fails closed) if no lockfile or bwrap is present.
Ensures detonate_live replaces the reactive stderr-driven loop with a single jailed lockfile installation attempt followed by a single re-run with PYTHONPATH updated to include the installed deps.
Retains injectable seams: pip_installer and jail_runner remain configurable parameters in detonate_live.
Preserves the existing 4-tuple/fs_snapshot_diff result shape and other detonation outputs.

spec.objective: Modify ngv2/poc_runner_live.py to replace host-side, un-jailed, stderr-driven reactive dependency installs with a secure, bwrap-jailed, network-unshared, lockfile-only dependency installer.
functional_requirements: Rebuild _default_pip_installer to resolve requirements.txt, requirements-dev.txt, or requirements.lock from the target's repo_root, failing closed (returning False) if none is found or if bwrap is missing.
Wrap the pip install argv using the module's own build_detonation_jail_argv to run with --unshare-net, read-only mapping the lockfile directory, and targeting target_dir as the write path.
Replace the reactive dependency installation loop in detonate_live with a single lockfile installation attempt using the injected pip_installer seam when the first run fails.
Modify detonate_live to perform a single re-run with target_dir/deps_dir appended to PYTHONPATH, bypassing any stderr module parsing for reactive fetching.
spec.interfaces: def _default_pip_installer(name: str, target_dir: str, python_bin: str='/usr/bin/python3') -> bool; def detonate_live(..., pip_installer=_default_pip_installer, jail_runner=...) -> tuple[bool, str, dict, dict] (keeping signature and injected seams).
edge_cases: Missing lockfile: fails closed (returns False, installs nothing).
bwrap check fails: returns False and logs warning when bwrap is not available.
Lockfile directory bindings: bind the directory containing the resolved lockfile read-only so bwrap can access it inside the jail.
non_goals: Do not touch workers, orchestration, conductor, run_hunt, or transition_planner.
Do not add support for npm / node_modules dependency installation.
Do not alter the semantic_verdict or fs_snapshot_diff validation mechanisms.
spec.implementation_notes:
SUBMISSION FORMAT: this is an io_adapter task. Emit a top-level __JANUSMASK_PATCHES__ list with exactly two kind:'symbol' entries: one replacing _default_pip_installer, one replacing detonate_live. You must set partial_edit: true in the task config. If a new sibling helper is added, R-anchor it on _default_pip_installer.

]

# CREDENTIAL-NAMING CONSTRAINT (the AST security gate FAILS the build if a variable whose name contains (case-insensitive) "password", "secret", or "key" is assigned a string literal -- it reads as a hardcoded credential even though this is an external clean-room target with no real secret). NEVER bind a string literal to such a variable. Use a neutral name instead (field_name, check_id, label, name, ident, column) or iterate a collection literal / build the mapping from a list of tuples. This applies to dict keys held in a temp var, field labels, and constant identifiers.

# STDLIB-ONLY CONSTRAINT (the verification environment installs NO third-party packages, so importing one fails collection -> the whole build is rolled back and the leaf is parked). Import ONLY the Python standard library. Import NO third-party package: NO pydantic, NO pydantic_settings, NO attrs, NO pyyaml, NO numpy, NO requests, etc. For data models / config use stdlib dataclasses (dataclasses.dataclass), enum.Enum, typing, and plain dict / json instead of pydantic BaseModel / BaseSettings. If the spec mentions pydantic-style validation, re-express it with stdlib dataclasses + manual checks.

# DETERMINISM CONSTRAINT (the AST nondeterminism gate FAILS the build if it sees a wall-clock or nondeterministic source). Do NOT call datetime.now / datetime.utcnow, time.time / time.monotonic, unseeded random, uuid, os.urandom, or secrets to obtain a timestamp / id / randomness. Instead accept any timestamp, seed, or clock as an EXPLICIT parameter with a deterministic default (the oracle injects it, e.g. via now_fn / make_scripted_clock), so the same inputs always produce the same output.
